title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. E is an elliptic curve in characteristic ≠ 2, given by the Weierstrass-type model z'^2 = f(z) = z^3 + a1 z^2 + a2 z + a3 = (z−ξ_i)(z−ξ_j)(z−ξ_k). The coordinates are z = ℘, z' = ℘' in a normalization without the factor 4. The three non-zero 2-torsion points ε_i ∈ I = ₂E(k)* satisfy ℘(ε_i) = ξ_i.

What the page does. It parametrizes, explicitly in coordinates, the following data: for each i ∈ I a half x_i of ε_i (2x_i = ε_i, eq. 67), subject to Σ_{i∈I} x_i = 0 (eq. 69). Grothendieck calls this the 'condition d'épinglage de Jacobi relatif d'échelon 4'.

Step 1 (z_i). Choose z_i = ℘(x_i). By the previous page, z_i is one of the two roots of (z_i−ξ_i)^2 = −(1/ξ_i)(a1 ξ_i^2 + 2a2 ξ_i + 3a3), eq. (65). These are the fixed points of the involution σ_i induced on the z-line by translation by ε_i.

Step 2 (z'_i). Choose z'_i = ℘'(x_i) with z'_i^2 = f(z_i), eq. (66). That gives 2 × 2 = 4 choices per i. This matches the fact that x_i is determined only up to ₂E(k), which has 4 elements.

Step 3 (the sum condition). Three distinct finite points of a plane cubic in Weierstrass form sum to 0 in the group law iff they are collinear. So Σx_i = 0 becomes the vanishing of det(1, z_i, z'_i), eq. (70). Expanded, this is the cyclic sum Σ (z_j z'_k − z_k z'_j) = 0. The next page names these terms ψ_i, indexed by a circular order ω on I.

Why the hypotheses hold. The x_i are pairwise distinct, and x_i ≠ ±x_j, since 2x_i = ε_i are distinct. Hence the z_i are distinct, no vertical line occurs, and the collinearity criterion ('prop. 3') applies.

Count. The set of solutions is a torsor under {(t_i) ∈ (₂E)^3 : Σ t_i = 0} ≅ (₂E)^2, so it has 16 elements. Existence: Σ 2x_i = ε1 + ε2 + ε3 = 0, so Σ x_i ∈ ₂E, and it can be corrected by changing one x_i.

Purpose. On the next page this explicit system (71) is to be used to attach to each such datum, functorially in E, an 'épi-flag de Legendre'. The work belongs to Grothendieck's program of explicit, canonically rigidified moduli of elliptic curves at levels 2 and 4 (Legendre/Jacobi forms, compatibility with a 'diagramme fondamental').
errors: No real error on this page. Two minor points from the previous page: the radicand in (65) is simply f'(ξ_i) = (ξ_i−ξ_j)(ξ_i−ξ_k) = 3ξ_i^2 + 2a1 ξ_i + a2 (equal modulo f(ξ_i) = 0). Using this form removes the division by ξ_i that worried Grothendieck in the margin; the classical halving formula z = ξ_i ± sqrt((ξ_i−ξ_j)(ξ_i−ξ_k)) follows directly.
Notation slip: in the factorization under (66), ζ is used where the previous page uses ξ for the roots ℘(ε_i).
The parenthetical 'cf prop. 3 ?' is unverified in the text. The criterion it invokes (three distinct points sum to zero iff collinear) is correct here, because the x_i are distinct and non-zero.

ideas.what: Coordinates of halves of a 2-torsion point: ℘(x) = ξ_i ± sqrt(f'(ξ_i)), followed by a choice of sign for ℘'(x); four choices, i.e. a ₂E-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Halving (2-descent) formulas on a Weierstrass cubic
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Weierstrass/Jacobi era; standard in Silverman, Knapp, Washington)

ideas.what: Condition that three points sum to zero expressed as collinearity, det(1, z_i, z'_i) = 0
Rigidifying datum: halves x_i of the three non-zero 2-torsion points with Σx_i = 0 (a torsor under (₂E)^2), called a 'relative Jacobi pinning of level 4'
ideas.modern_name: Level-(2,4)-type structure / Jacobi-quartic rigidification over a Legendre (level 2) structure
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses modular towers in general but not this specific datum, as far as I know

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but classical coordinate computation: halving 2-torsion points and expressing Σx_i = 0 as a collinearity determinant. Its only distinctive feature is Grothendieck's private terminology ('épinglage de Jacobi relatif d'échelon 4', 'épi-flag de Legendre') within a broader unpublished program on explicit rigidified moduli. Nothing on this page itself looks new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: In (66) the underbrace factorization is written with the root symbols ζ_i, ζ_j, ζ_k (the same roots called ξ on the previous page); the transcription is otherwise faithful.
'(2 choix possibles)' is written above '(65), et ensuite' and refers to the choice of z_i in (68a); the transcription places it correctly.
Last lines read '(cf prop. 3 ?, qui s'applique, car les x_i sont tous distincts...)'; the transcription is correct.
